Rajesh Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 22
September, 2017
 1

High Court Of Madhya Pradesh, Principal Seat At Jabalpur
 (Single Bench : Hon'Ble Shri Justice J.P.Gupta)
 M.Cr.C.No. 2722/ 2006
 Rajesh Kumar and two others
 Vs.
 State of Madhya Pradesh
Shri Surendra Singh, learned Senior Advocate with Shri Ashwani
Dubey, Advocate for the petitioners.
Shri R. N. Yadav, Panel Lawyer for the respondents-State.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Whether approved for reporting : (Yes / No).
 ORDER (Delivered on 22 day of September, 2017) nd The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashment of the proceedings of criminal case no.
4/05 registered on the complaint filed by the Food Inspector, Sagar, with regard to commission of offence under Section 7 (2) (9) K read with section 16 (1) and Rule 50 read with section 7 (3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 alleging that on 24.10.1997 the complainant / Food Inspector, inspected a shop of peti- tioner no. 1 Rajesh and seized a packet of "SIL" Pineapple Jam which was misbranded and did not contain expiry date of the food article which is violation of Rule 32 (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules 1955 and the petitioners no. 2 and 3 were manufacturer of the product.
Apart form it, the petitioners no. 2 and 3 were failed to pro- duce license for selling of food articles which is also violation of Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.
2. The aforesaid proceedings have been challenged mainly on the ground that the provisions of Rule 32 (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 was not in existence on 24.10.1997.
Therefore, no question for violation of the Rules arises.

Similarly, Rule 50 of the Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 is not applicable as the Jam is a food arti- cle which comes in purview of Food Products Order, 1955 and by provi- so to the said Rules such articles have been exempted.

In such circum- stances, the proceeding of the prosecution of petitioner no. 1 as a Sell- er and petitioners no. 2 and 3 as the Directors of Manufacturer Compa- ny of the Product are bad in law and misuse of process of the court.
Hence, the proceedings be quashed.
3. Learned PL has opposed the aforesaid contentions and prayed for rejection of the petition.

4. Having considered the contentions of learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record,

sentences.text: the contentions of the learned counsel for the petitioners have substance as Rule 32 (i) has been insert- ed by GSR 380 (E) dated 25.6.1998 (w.e.f.9.7.1998) and before that there was no rule (i) and there was no provision in any other rule with regard to mentioning of expiry date of the product and inspection was made on 24.10.1997.
Therefore, no seller or manufacturer can be prose- cuted for violation of the rules which were not in existence at the rele- vant time.
Learned trial Court and the revisional Court have ignored the aforesaid legal aspect of the case.
5. So far as the violation of Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 is concerned

,
it is itself provided that if the product comes under the Fruit Products Order, 1955 apart from oth- er products shall be exempted from the above Rules.

The Fruit Products Order, 1955 is issued in exercise of powers conferred by Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 by SRO 1052 dated 3.5.1955 and amend- ed by SO 5593 dated 30.12.1971 Column no. 2 (cc) defined "fruit product",
prescribed (vi) "jams" as a Fruit Product covered by the Or- der.
Therefore, Rule 50 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 is not attracted in the case and this aspect has also been over- looked by the courts below.
6. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the prosecution of the petitioners is contrary to law and misuse of process of the court.

Hence, the petition is allowed and the proceedings of criminal case no. 4/05 pending against the petitioners with regard to commission of of- fence under Section 7 (2)
(9) K read with section 16 (1) and Rule 50 read with section 7 (3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
are hereby quashed.
7. A copy of this order be sent to the concerned court below for information and its compliance.

(J.P.GUPTA) JUDGE JP/-
